name: Beef, Australian, imported, grass-fed, round, bottom round steak/roast, boneless, separable lean and fat, raw (USDA food medium)
description: Food-derived medium from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy): measured amino acids, sugars, fatty acids, vitamins and minerals of Beef, Australian, imported, grass-fed, round, bottom round steak/roast, boneless, separable lean and fat, raw, plus a mineral base. Measured nutrients with no curated BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered; non-metabolite aggregates (energy, protein, total fat/fibre) are excluded by design.

provenance.citation: U.S. Department of Agriculture, FoodData Central (SR Legacy), fdc.nal.usda.gov (FDC ID 173976).
provenance.notes: USDA measured nutrients mapped to BiGG via a curated nutrient->exchange table; amounts (per 100 g) in usda_amount/usda_unit. Unmapped measured metabolites kept in uncovered (v2). Aggregates excluded.
provenance.license_name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication
provenance.url_status_note: USDA FoodData Central returns HTTP 404 for food-details URLs while its single-page app renders the correct food page client-side (verified 2026-09-06: curl -> 404 with an identical app shell for every id; headless Chromium -> the correct title and nutrient table). The link works for a reader and fails for a link-checker. Do not retire it.

components.mapping_note: source name destroyed at build time; it was one of Cystine / Cysteine and the two collide on this exchange; build_usda_media_v2.py NMAP_RAW; [CHEM-CYS-01] USDA nutrient 1216 "Cystine" is L-cystine, the disulfide DIMER (C6H12N2O4S2, InChIKey LEVWYRKDKASIDU-IMJSIDKUSA-N, BiGG id cysi__L). It was mapped to cys__L, L-cysteine, the MONOMER (C3H7NO2S, XUJNEKJLAYXESH-REOHCLBHSA-N) -- a different skeleton and 2x stoichiometry -- and stamped "exact". The two USDA nutrients "Cystine" and "Cysteine" additionally collide on the same exchange key, so one measured amount silently overwrote the other. The source nutrient name was destroyed at build time (the record stores the BiGG name), so which of the two produced any given row is UNRECOVERABLE from the shipped data: the row cannot be retargeted, only relabelled and flagged. Correct target for future builds is cysi__L; see tools/curation/usda_nutrient_table.tsv.

components.mapping_note: source name destroyed at build time; it was one of MUFA 18:1 c / MUFA 18:1 and the two collide on this exchange; build_usda_media_v2.py NMAP_RAW; [CLASS-USDA-181] USDA reaches ocdcea only through the class strings "MUFA 18:1 c" and "MUFA 18:1", both of which name a chain-length:unsaturation CLASS covering every C18:1 positional and geometric isomer. The builder replaced the class string with the BiGG display name "Octadecenoate (n-C18:1)", so the rows are invisible to a name-based rule and are matched on method plus id. BiGG resolves six distinct C18:1 species, so the collapse onto oleate is a declared assumption. The two source nutrients also collide on this one exchange, so one measured amount silently overwrote the other.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
